newsitem.title: UK: British drivers tempted by road rage urged to pray.
newsitem.headline: British drivers tempted by road rage urged to pray.

text.p: British drivers who might be tempted by what the media has dubbed "road rage" are being offered a Christian highway code to help them turn the other cheek to aggressive behaviour.
The Christian Road Safety Association has published its 10 commandments for peace on the roads, the Times newspaper reported in its Thursday edition.
The association said it was concerned at an apparent rise in incidents of road rage on Britain's highways, where some disputes between drivers have resulted in murder.
The new 10 commandments for the road are:
-- If you start late, arrive late.
-- Alcohol is for the radiator, not the operator.
-- If entry into the flow of traffic is facilitated by the courtesy of another driver, wave in appreciation.
-- If you have inadvertently endangered the safe passage of an another vehicle, wave as an apology.
-- Make it easy for aggressive opportunity snatchers to get ahead of you -- far ahead.
-- Drive so that the sudden appearance of a police patrol car is a pleasant sight.
-- Give plenty of space to cars marked with dents.
-- Never accelerate, and decelerate if advisable, when another car wishes to enter your lane.
-- End every trip with a prayer of thanksgiving.
